To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
type III collagen is coordinately expressed with type I collagen and that this expression is regulated by the growth state of the cell.
the expression of the three collagen genes is coordinately modulatd during fibroblast proliferation.
the expression of type III collagen is regulated in a similar manner as that of the type II collagen genes, and that the regulation of these three genes is independent of their chromosomal location.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the type I and III collagens.
the regulation of the expression of the genes encoding human collagen type III.
the molecular mechanisms involved in the expression of collagen genes during the growth cycle of human fibroblasts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alpha 2(I), alpha 1(II), and alpha 1(IV) collagen genes are not coordinately regulated during fibroblast proliferation and differentiation.
the alpha 2(I), alpha 1(II), and alpha 1(IV) mRNAs were coordinately regulated in a manner consistent with the hypothesis that their expression was regulated at the level of transcription.
, during fibroblast proliferation, the expression of type III collagen is coordinately modulatd with the expression of the alpha 1 and alpha 2 genes of type I collagen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the alpha 2(III) and alpha 1(I)-alpha 2(I) mRNAs are coordinately modulated in a manner that is independent of the alpha 1 (III) mRNA.
type III collagen gene is coordinately regulated with the type I genes.

, during periods of rapid growth, the type III collagen mRNA levels were reduced to about one-half of their steady-state level, whereas during periods of slow growth, the type I collagen mRNA levels were increased about two- and threefold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of type III collagen and the type I collagen chains are coordinately regulated.

the alpha 3(IV) collagen mRNA is a major component of the mRNA population expressed during periods of slow and rapid fibroblast growth, and that this mRNA is coordinately regulated with alpha 1(I)- and alpha 2(II)-specific mRNA transcripts.
, in human lung fibroblast cells, the type III collagen genes are coordinately modulated in a similar way to that of the alpha 1 and alpha 2 chains of type I collagen.
